coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: China Basin Park
record.summary: The waterfront park that the Port's June 2026 report lists among Mission Rock's completed Phase 1 elements as the '5-acre China Basin Park' (other Port documents give its size as 4.4 acres in 2018 and 'almost five acres' in 2025); SF YIMBY reports that SCAPE Studio was responsible for its master design and that Webcor was the general contractor. An opening celebration was held on the morning before SF YIMBY's April 26, 2024 article. The Port says the City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure, including parks.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry (DataSF Assessor lot 8719A005) with one documented exclusion: the ~1,660 m2 Block K lobe, cut along the lot's own recorded vertices. High confidence on the boundary; the K cut is the only edited edge.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 8719A005 (recorded 2020-06-12, mapped 2021-04-13, active), minus the lobe the plan's Block K occupies; cross-checked against OpenStreetMap way 27656676 (leisure=park, name=China Basin Park) and Mission Rock Design Controls Figures 1.1 (p.10) and 3.2.1 (p.47).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The park's lot 8719A005 exists and is active, but it still contains the unbuilt Block K's land; joining status.csv to it would draw the park over a planned block.
notes.regulatory_context: Dedicated public open space, Design Controls Section 3.2: three programme 'rooms' (Plaza, Play Area, Great Lawn) linked by a Waterfront Promenade carrying the Bay Trail / Blue Greenway; Public Trust use; a Park Promenade at least 24 ft wide in front of Blocks A, G and K.

changes.text: The Port's June 2026 report lists the '5-acre China Basin Park' among Phase 1's completed elements; the Port's January 2018 staff report gives 4.4 acres and its February 2025 minutes say 'almost five acres'. The Port's October 2023 memo lists a Phase 1 budget line for the inland park of $39.2 to $40.7 million (revised estimates, not a final cost). That memo also says 'in-water' work was delayed to a later phase; no source read says whether any park shoreline or in-water work remains.

Long 'At a glance' values were cut to the fact itself (or 'Sources differ'); the disputes, quoted excerpts and hedging moved to this record's open questions, with every source still named. No change to the record's status or shape.

The China Basin Park timeline now says that SF YIMBY reported on June 3, 2022 that construction had started with a groundbreaking ceremony; that is the article's publication date, and no source gives the ceremony's date.

open_questions: No cost for the park as a whole is published in any source read. The Port's October 6, 2023 memo (Table 1, Expected Final Budget) has a Phase 1 hard-cost line labelled 'Inland CBP' of $27,397,300 (2019 approved budget), $33,395,979 (2021 approved budget) and $39,184,050 to $40,657,253 (revised low and high estimates). These are budget figures, not final costs, and the table shows no separate line for shoreline or in-water work.
The Port's 5-acre figure and the mapped lot area differ; which boundary the Port counts is not stated.

The Port's October 2023 memo says the 2021 Phase 1 budget increases did not include 'in-water' work 'being delayed to a later phase', and describes 'a revised schedule for the construction of China Basin Park inland and shoreline components'. No source read says whether any park shoreline or in-water work remains outstanding.

Area of China Basin Park: the Port's June 2026 staff report says 'the 5-acre China Basin Park'; earlier Port documents say '4.4 acre China Basin Park' (January 26, 2018 staff report) and 'almost five acres' (staff remarks, February 11, 2025 minutes). Pier & Point's mapped lot 8719A005 is about 4.69 acres less the Block K lobe, so the figures are not directly comparable.
